findings.title: T-9 and T-10 cannot show they are done
quotes: - Mode: direct: skill text, checked later by T-12's test
- Mode: single: text edit and its substring test are one small change
findings.fix: give T-9 and T-10 their own substring check over their file, or mode them single like T-2.

sources.situation: the worker of T-10 adds the blocked-handoff offer to skills/implement/SKILL.md and reports done. TC-16 is only written by T-12, which depends on T-9 and T-10, so nothing runs when T-10 closes. If the implement skill lacks "Escalating a bug fix", the miss shows up only at T-12, after T-10 is closed, and no task owns the fix. Other text-edit tasks (T-2, T-6, T-8, T-11) are moded single so their own substring test runs in the same task.

findings.reason: T-9 and T-10 are `Mode: direct` with `Test: TC-16`, but tests.md says TC-16 is written in T-12 (`test_lite_skill_texts`), which depends on both, so nothing runs when they close. T-12's `Files` is only `tests/test_flow.py`, so a miss in `skills/implement/SKILL.md` or `skills/tasks/SKILL.md` found there falls outside any task's files, while T-2, T-6, T-8 and T-11 are `single` and check their own text.
findings.note: T-9 and T-10 are single, each adding its own file's TC-16 check; T-12 keeps the grill and drafter card

findings.title: One test function is marked new by five tasks
findings.fix: name T-2 as the creator and mark the other tasks as adding a check to the existing function.

sources.situation: T-2 (TC-2), T-6 (TC-8), T-8 (TC-12), T-11 (TC-13 to TC-15) and T-12 (TC-16) each name tests/test_flow.py:test_lite_skill_texts, and each TC entry says "(new)". T-6 and T-8 depend only on T-1, so nothing orders them after T-2. A worker of T-8 who runs first creates the function, and T-2's worker then creates it again or overwrites it.

findings.note: T-2 creates test_lite_skill_texts; T-6, T-8, T-9, T-10, T-11, T-12 add to it, ordered after T-2

findings.title: Existing lite-route assertions change and no task says so
quotes: `kind(root, slug)` returns `effort` for `route: full` and `route: lite`
findings.fix: name the two existing assertions in T-1 as to be updated to the new behaviour.

sources.situation: in tests/test_flow.py, two existing assertions expect a lite spec to be unsupported: flow.kind returns "unsupported: lite" (around line 170), and next_step prints "unsupported: lite: nio flow drives full-route specs only" (around line 608). After T-1, CT-2 makes both wrong. No task names these assertions, so a worker of T-1 either leaves the suite red or edits them without being asked. This is inferred from the code, not quoted from the pack.

findings.note: T-1's title names the existing lite-unsupported assertions it moves to an epic spec
